transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-23
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 mins
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Sable Head of Data), Kevin Cho (Sable Platform Eng), Derek Neal (Sable CTO)
Recording ID: ff-20260423-sable-poc-001

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 6-week POC to validate inference economics and latency for Sable's alerting/resolution workflow. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, required access, kickoff timeline, mid-point review, and exec readout. Action items captured at end.

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, quality thresholds)
- Workload sizing and sample datasets
- Benchmark methodology and tooling (end-to-end, p99 latency, tail, streaming)
- Security/access (VPC, IAM role, logs retention)
- Timeline: kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um this is Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. i'll let lina jump in for the technical bit after a quick framing.
[00:12] Marta: thanks Samir, appreciate it. we’ve been evaluating a few inference options for our incident classification pipeline, mainly curious on latency and cost tradeoffs.
[00:20] Lina: great, hi all. lina gomez, solutions engineer. quick agenda: confirm success criteria, get workload numbers, agree benchmark plan, and lock milestones. sound good?
[00:28] Derek: yep, quick note — timeline is important, we have an exec review on the 18th of May so would like a readout before then.
[00:36] Samir: perfect, we'll aim to align. can we start with success criteria — what would constitute a successful POC for you?
[00:43] Marta: three things: 1) p99 latency under 350ms for our short prompt path, 2) cost per 1k tokens below our current baseline (~$2.50 per 1k), and 3) quality parity — less than 5% regression on our classification F1 compared to current model.
[00:58] Kevin: and from infra, must be demonstrably deployable in our VPC with KMS integration and audit logs turned on. also need RBAC for access.
[01:10] Lina: makes sense. couple clarifications — when you say p99 350ms, is that for single-request synchronous calls for prompts of ~120 tokens?
[01:18] Marta: yes, typical prompt is 80–150 tokens. we also have a heavy batch path for nightly reranks but latency there is less critical.
[01:26] Samir: and traffic profile? kevin, you mentioned earlier a spike pattern?
[01:31] Kevin: yeah, base is 200 qps avg during business hours, spikes to 800 for 2–3 minutes occasionally, overall sustained daily tokens around ~10M tokens/day peak. the pilot can sample down to 200k–1M tokens/day for the bench. i can share more exact traces.
[01:47] Lina: ok that's helpful. for the POC we usually do two benchmark runs — a synthetic steady-state to validate latency and throughput, and an end-to-end run using a 24–72 hour trace you provide to validate cost and tail latencies.
[01:58] Derek: is that the same harness you used for the Orion bench you published? i remember a spreadsheet.
[02:03] Lina: yes similar; we have an internal benchmark harness and a public repo link we can share. note that on some calls the runtime name is transcribed oddly — it's Redwood Dedicaed in notes sometimes, but it's Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private depending on deployment.
[02:17] Samir: ha, yeah transcriptions love that one.
[02:20] Marta: about deployment mode — we want to test both Hosted API and a Dedicated pool. hosted is for quick comparison, dedicated for economics if we get to volume. you mentioned Private for VPC?
[02:31] Lina: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed into a VPC with customer-managed KMS. for the POC we can run an isolated Dedicated cluster in our cloud account or run Private in your account — tradeoffs: Dedicated in our infra is faster to stand up, Private in your VPC gives you full network isolation and simpler compliance review.
[02:47] Kevin: speed to stand up is critical; we prefer dedicated in Redwood infra to start, but we need a clear path to VPC for the security team.
[02:55] Samir: noted. milestones — i'll propose a 6-week plan: week 0 kickoff & access, week 1 bench setup, weeks 2–3 run baseline benchmarks and tuning, week 4 mid-point review with preliminary results, week 5 tuning & extended runs, week 6 exec readout and handover.
[03:15] Derek: that corresponds to our needs if the exec readout is scheduled for May 15th week.
[03:21] Lina: operational tasks for week 0: you give us an AWS role or temp creds for the benchmark runner, plus a test dataset and traffic trace. we request a VPN or peered VPC for Private, but for Dedicated we just need IAM and network egress rules.
[03:36] Kevin: who's responsible for the IAM role on our side? that's mine, i can create an assumption role and share.
[03:40] Samir: perfect. lina will send a template for the least-privilege role.
[03:45] Marta: about quality testing, how do you track quality regressions? can you run our eval tests as part of the harness?
[03:51] Lina: yes, we can run your evaluation suite against outputs. just send the eval scripts or the label set and we'll integrate. we also provide prompt/response diffing and a simple drift dashboard.
[04:03] Derek: do you support KV cache warmup or prefix caching? some of our long-conversation cases rely on that for latency.
[04:10] Lina: yes, runtime supports KV cache management and prefix caching; note caching behavior can change latency profiles for the first few tokens. we'll capture warm and cold p99s.
[04:19] Marta: what about model variants and quantization — can we test a quantized variant to reduce cost?
[04:25] Lina: absolutely, part of Redwood Optimize we can suggest quant profiles. for the bench we'll run both fp16-like builds and a 4-bit quantized path, compare quality and cost.
[04:35] Samir: any compliance docs you need early — SOC 2, ISO, or just SOC 2 is enough for your team?
[04:41] Derek: SOC 2 report and details on encryption at rest plus KMS integration. also audit log retention policy — we asked for 1 year minimum.
[04:49] Samir: will include security pack link in follow-up.
[04:52] Kevin: for benchmarks, are you running at scale in our account or in Redwood's cloud? we prefer runs from our region to get realistic latency.
[04:59] Lina: we can deploy benchmark runners in your region using the IAM role. for Dedicated-in-Redwood we can co-locate in the same cloud region to mimic production.
[05:08] Marta: what's the expected runtime to stand up dedicated environment?
[05:11] Lina: typically 3–5 business days once we have access; Private in your VPC is more like 1–2 weeks because of networking and security reviews.
[05:19] Derek: ok that fits.
[05:21] Samir: summary and proposed dates: Kickoff target week of 2026-04-27 (that's next week), Bench setup complete by 2026-05-04, Mid-point review 2026-05-11, Exec readout 2026-05-15. That compresses to 3 weeks, we may slide mid-point to week 3 for 6-week total but given your exec date we can do a shorter demo.
[05:41] Marta: let's try the tight cadence — we'll prioritize the samples.
[05:45] Kevin: i'll share the traffic trace and a small sample dataset (3k rows) by Monday 2026-04-26.
[05:52] Lina: i'll post the benchmark harness repo and the IAM role template in the notes. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness (placeholder)
[05:59] Derek: any major risks?
[06:01] Lina: main risks are data sensitivity delays for getting access, and model quality regressions on quantized variants. we'll highlight those in the SOW and mitigation steps.
[06:10] Samir: ok action items — i'll go through them.
[06:14] Marta: quick pricing question — do you have a pilot price or trial credit?
[06:18] Samir: we have a pilot discount for POCs; i'll include the pricing sheet in the follow-up.
[06:23] Kevin: competitors — FYI security team also asked us to compare Anthropic and AWS Bedrock for a cost baseline.
[06:30] Samir: understood, we can include a quick cost compare with our baseline numbers.
[06:34] Lina: any other open questions?
[06:36] Marta: none for now. we'll wait for the SOW.
[06:39] Samir: great. recap of next steps: 1) Samir to send SOW + pricing + security pack, 2) Kevin to send traces and small dataset, 3) Lina to send bench harness link and IAM template, 4) schedule kickoff for week of 4/27.
[06:55] Derek: thanks everyone.
[06:57] Marta: thanks.
[06:58] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and hub. bye.

End of transcript.

References mentioned:
